newsitem.title: USA: Wyman-Gordon to pay $1.8 mln over fatal accident.
newsitem.headline: Wyman-Gordon to pay $1.8 mln over fatal accident.

text.p: Wyman-Gordon Forgings Inc has agreed to pay $1.8 million in penalties following a December 1996 accident at its Houston facility that killed eight workers and injured two others, the Occupational Safety and Health Administration said Wednesday.
The company and its affiliate, Wyman-Gordon Company, Inc., also agreed to make "significant" safety improvements at five U.S. plants, OSHA reported.

The agreement follows a December 22 incident in which an unexpected release of pressurized nitrogen killed four production and four maintenance workers and injured two others. The force of the released nitrogen was so strong it propelled a 3,000 pound valve assembly over 200 yards.
"We must insist that safety and health be as important to a company as earnings and market share," Labor Secretary Alexis Herman said in a statement.

North Grafton, Mass.-based Wyman-Gordon Forgings, Inc., manufactures forgings, investment castings and composite air frame structures and is a major supplier to the aircraft and aerospace industries. About 865 people are employed at the Houston plant and Wyman-Gordon Company, Inc., employs more than 3,000 people worldwide.
